historical_commentary.text: This note shows how to send authenticated SMTP email from 4D using the SMTP_Auth command from the 4D Internet Commands plug-in, wrapping the simpler (but non-authenticating) SMTP_QuickSend command in a new Email_QuickSend method that adds a password parameter. 4D Internet Commands and this specific command set have since been superseded by 4D's built-in, natively supported SMTP commands, and the simple username/password SMTP authentication model shown here predates the OAuth2-based authentication that most modern mail providers now require.
related_updates: 4D Internet Commands (a separate plug-in in this era) was eventually folded into or replaced by native 4D language commands for email/network protocols in later 4D versions
Most major email providers (Gmail, Office 365, etc.) have since deprecated simple username/password SMTP authentication in favor of OAuth2, which this note's technique does not address
Modern 4D applications typically use 4D's native SMTP-related commands or third-party REST-based transactional email APIs rather than 4D Internet Commands' SMTP_Auth
